name: Captain Geutler
summary: The captain Larry would call when he wanted to get out: "Rosethorn 007 was a aircraft call sign I would use. It was the helicopter that we had access to. When I wanted to get out of here, I would call Captain Guetler." Larry names him in uniform at the Huey in VN-0020: "He was in his late 50s and was in the military a long time," and he always heard the captain was a great pilot. On his last day on the mountain, Larry says, it was this captain who came for him: "captain Geutler (his spelling) came and got me and dropped off Sgt Weaver." Looking at VN-0016 on 2026-09-12 he placed him at the controls, hedged: "Geutler was the guy flying possibly to the left of Estes."
researchNotes: Display name changed 2026-09-14 from Captain "Guegler" to Geutler, the one rendering Larry spelled himself; the slug stays captain-guegler and every rendering stays in aliases. SPELLING PROVENANCE, corrected 2026-09-02: of the five renderings held here, only "Geutler" is Larry's own. His son wrote it into the record as "captain Geutler (his spelling)" and confirmed afterwards that he had asked Larry directly and Larry spelled it that way. The other four are his son's transcriptions of the name as Larry says it, made at different times, and they are not independent evidence of how Larry renders the name. Roster searches should lead with Geutler; other candidates to search alongside it: Guegler, Guetler, Gutler, Getler, Gugler, Geigler, Giegler, Kugler. A captain in his late fifties implies prior-enlisted or WWII/Korea service, which narrows roster searches. Magnification (2026-08-15) settled an earlier tension: the tape once read as possibly beginning 'J' is the standard U.S. ARMY tape below aviator wings, so nothing in the photo contradicts the identification; his own name tape is hidden behind the jacket panel. He is the named pilot of the extraction on the last day (data/recollections/giscus-stories-c18259364.json), though nothing documentary ties him to the later killed-in-action report. The VN-0016 placement (giscus-vn-0016-c18415765) is hedged "possibly", so the frame is not linked to this record. Further identity notes: research/people/captain-guegler.md.
